question_text: How do you calculate the efficiency of an LDO, and how does it differ from a buck converter?
explanation_text: Because an LDO doesn't switch, the input current is essentially identical to the output current (ignoring a tiny quiescent ground current). Therefore, the efficiency is simply the ratio of the voltages. If you drop 5V to 3.3V, the efficiency is 3.3 / 5 = 66%. The remaining 34% of the power is burned entirely as heat.
bonus_question_text: When can an LDO actually be highly efficient?
bonus_answer_text: When the input voltage is very close to the output voltage (e.g., dropping 3.5V to 3.3V yields ~94% efficiency).
